title: Nine Pages of Writing
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：chapter　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chapter 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 my mother was sent to write ① chapter she could not finish, and she said the writing was the whole of the lesson. The ② chapter, meaning the section and not the book, was nine pages long and was written by whoever came last; chapter, she said, is the only thing in a book that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chapter in that book had the same ending, and the ④ chapter at the end, meaning the one the editor kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever wrote properly. Chapter, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chapter was the whole of the novel, meaning the period it carried and not the section. The ⑥ chapter, meaning the period and not any of that, is the only thing in a novel that everybody remembers and nobody questions; chapter, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a section and a period. She said the period is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ chapter had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the ending. The ⑧ chapter of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine pages and eleven years of writing; chapter, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chapter I remember is the one at the end, which was written in 1976 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ chapter, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being written; every chapter, she said, is a period that has agreed to look like a section. She said the period was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 章节（指那一节本身，与整本书相对）
C. 固定搭配：write a chapter 写一章
D. n. 章节（指那本书里每一章）
E. n. 章节（指末尾那一章）
F. n. 阶段（抽象：它承载的那段时期）
G. n. 那段时期（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chapter, meaning the section and not the book
chapter was the whole of the novel
the chapter had become a number in a report
The chapter of the whole thing
A chapter, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: write a chapter 意为“写一章”，1956 年母亲被派去写她写不完的那一章。
chapter 意为“章、章节”，指那一节本身而不是整本书，共九页，由最后来的人写。
chapter 指那本书里每一章，每一章都是同样的结尾。
chapter 指末尾那一章（编辑保留的那一章），是唯一有人认真写过的。
chapter 意为“阶段”，抽象指它承载的那段时期，父亲说 chapter 就是那部长篇的全部。
chapter 为抽象用法，指那段时期本身，是一部小说里人人都记得、却没人质疑的东西。
chapter 意为“章、章节”，到 1971 年这一章成了报告里的一个数字。
chapter 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九页和十一年的写作。
chapter 意为“章节”，我记得的是末尾那一章，1976 年写成，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
chapter 为抽象总称，祖母说一章文字是唯一会因为被认真写作而变好的东西。
